basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 23:2 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 211. Cur una civitas Hebron tribus appellata est nominibus, videlicet, Hebron,'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 211. Cur una civitas Hebron tribus appellata est nominibus, videlicet, Hebron, Arbe, [et] Mambre (Gen. XXIII, 2)?-- Resp. Hebron [civitas] a Gigantibus, a quibus quondam condita est: et Arbe a numero, videlicet quatuor, [habet nomen], quod ibi quatuor patriarchae sepulti sunt; Adam magnus humani generis pater; Abraham, [et] Isaac [et] Jacob. Haec eadem a quodam amicorum Abraham Mambre vocata est.
